decision.detail: I'm already sitting up. Boots on the floor, one sock half on. I pull the second sock, yank on the windbreaker I wore yesterday, dig the coach ticket out of the inside pocket where I folded it last time. The paper's creased. I don't care. I swing my bag over my shoulder, open the door to the lobby, and I'm past the coffee table, past the coat-check stand where that envelope sits, past the two crew members still arguing about whether the pastry case counts as a breakfast concession. I don't stop. I don't need to stop. My legs already know the route to the lot. The van that backfired is still idling. I don't look at it.
decision.intention: Be in Pittsburgh on that coach. Be at my sister's door before eight on Wednesday. Couch goes through the door, not the window. I don't need a piano lesson or a reel of film or a flat tire fixed to do this. I need to be on a moving vehicle for roughly four hours and then I need to be where the couch is. That's the whole plan. That's the whole day. The radio will still say Tuesday when I wake up and I'll still be in the hotel and I'll still be doing this. Fine. I'll do it. I'll do it until the couch is on the other side of the hallway and my sister isn't looking at me like I'm a broken promise. The ticket is paid. The seat is there. I sit in it.
decision.words: "Coach is at nine. I've got a couch in Pittsburgh on Wednesday. Be seeing you."
